evidence.field: description; source; reuse rights; script classification
evidence.text: Commons identifies this as a digitally created vector depicting 菜 in the Shuowen seal-script style and names Sinica, Chinese Etymology, CUHK’s Multi-function Chinese Character Database, Chinese Text Project, and Chinese Linguipedia as source databases. The file description calls the image public domain and says attribution is appreciated but not required. It is a modern redraw of a historical script form, not an artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:菜-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: 字形; form inventory and account of graphic structure
evidence.text: The entry displays a seal form and six bronze examples, with one slip-text example; its account parses 菜 as 艸 plus phonetic 采 and cites Qin-slip 采(菜)羹. The page has no oracle-bone form in its displayed inventory. These page descriptions support the form-history context for considering the seal-style redraw, but do not establish a specific date or provenance for the Commons vector itself.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 菜

evidence.text: The source page links the original vector file as a direct SVG image. The web tool could not open that direct upload URL; the file-description page itself identifies the image and its rights.
evidence.title: 菜-seal.svg (original file)

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 菜 seal script character glyph 菜 file; Wikimedia Commons 菜 oracle bone bronze script 菜 character; 菜 字形 漢語多功能字庫 字形 圖片
search_audit.outcome: Searched and opened the Commons file page, CUHK character entry, and Sinica character page. The Commons page describes a Shuowen seal-style image and gives reuse rights; CUHK displays historical forms and component analysis. The Sinica evolution link failed to fetch.

search_audit.query: Commons variants for 菜 seal glyph; direct searches for 菜-bronze.svg and 菜 Qin slip glyph
search_audit.outcome: Opened the linked Commons script categories and searched for character-specific bronze and Qin-slip files. No character-specific Commons candidate was established for those periods. The seal file page lists several script variants, but links for Shang oracle and bronze variants lead to general categories, not confirmed 菜 images.

search_audit.query: Open direct Wikimedia Commons upload URL for 菜-seal.svg
search_audit.outcome: Direct upload URL was inaccessible through the web tool. The Commons description page was inspected and is sufficient for image identity and reuse provenance; no pixel inspection was performed.

gaps: Only one directly supported, reusable candidate was established: a modern vector redraw of a seal-script form. No ancient artifact photograph or verified bronze/Qin-slip glyph image with individual provenance and reuse information was established in this search.
The Commons file page names source databases, but this research did not independently verify the exact source specimen behind the specific seal-form drawing.

The Sinica character-history page opened, but its evolution subpage failed with a cache-miss error. CUHK’s entry showed form categories and counts but does not provide specimen dating in the inspected text.
No visual inspection of the candidate image was performed; the image page description and provenance were used only to propose it for subsequent pixel review.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector drawing uploaded 2024-10-29. The graphic page does not specify the seal specimen’s exact historical date.
items.tradition: Chinese seal script as represented in the Shuowen tradition
items.caption: A modern redraw of 菜 in Shuowen seal-script style. Shuowen analyzes the graph as 艸 with 采 supplying the sound; this image is a script-style reconstruction, not a photograph of an ancient inscription.
items.alt: Black seal-style form of 菜, reproduced as a square vector glyph on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The Commons description explicitly identifies the character and script style, names ancient-character reference databases, and records public-domain reuse. The CUHK entry separately documents a seal-form example and the 艸 plus 采 analysis. This gives a sourced candidate illustrating the later formal presentation of the graph.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the modern SVG representation of an ancient script; Commons says attribution is appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: This is a modern redraw, not an ancient object photograph. Its specific model specimen and date are not given on the Commons page; the page only identifies Shuowen seal-script style and lists source databases. No verified, rights-cleared individual bronze or Qin-slip glyph image was found in this search.

The direct SVG upload URL could not be opened by the web tool, and the image pixels were not inspected. The candidate is proposed based on the opened description page, with final visual validation left to the stated review process.
